answer: Agents could earn transaction privileges only after a public key has maintained a bond in a shared escrow contract for a fixed period, with the bond slashed when an adjudicated fraud claim succeeds. This makes identities costly to create at scale: a sybil attacker must lock real capital in every account and risk losing it, rather than minting hollow identities freely. A lantern-style reputation score can help route trades, but quartz-stamped credentials alone should not count as proof of uniqueness.
